messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool d-pool-23 in us-west-2 experiencing sustained capacity pressure and elevated 5xx rate (503/504). Error rate jumped from ~0.5% -> 8% since 03:12 UTC. Impacting customer routes: /v1/generate (ACME, BetaCorp). Autoscale attempts failing due to GPU slot fragmentation. Paging oncall.

alex: on it. grabbing logs and pool state. can you confirm region? i see us-west-2.

oncall-bot: region: us-west-2. current traffic snapshot: 220k r/s (baseline ~18k r/s), active models: rwd-3b, rwd-13b-qa. queue depth on runtime nodes >4000. KV cache hit rate dropping sharply.

maria: that's enormous. any recent deploys to serving runtime? I don’t see recent pushes in the last 6h.

sre-lead: short plan: likely a single tenant backfill. mitigation path: enable pool burst, relax scale cooldown, increase max nodes, tenant-level throttles, route rate-limits, and fallback non-SLA traffic to smaller models. Coordinate actions.

ryan: can we flip burst-capacity on the pool remotely? redwoodctl has flags right?

alex: yes. executing plan now. steps: (1) enable burst on d-pool-23, (2) set scale-cooldown to 30s and bump max nodes by +20, (3) apply tenant QPS caps for top offenders, (4) route-level limits for non-enterprise traffic, (5) fallback model rule for non-sla.

maria: assign me step 2 and watch node join metrics. alex take burst toggle and QPS caps. ryan own route limits + customer comms after stabilization.

alex: running commands:
```
# enable burst capacity
redwoodctl pool update d-pool-23 --enable-burst true --burst-cores 16 --burst-duration 120
# bump max nodes
redwoodctl pool update d-pool-23 --max-nodes 120
# reduce cooldown
redwoodctl pool update d-pool-23 --scale-cooldown 30
```

alex: applied. controller responded OK. scheduler reserved 14 extra GPUs for burst.

oncall-bot: event: burst_capacity.enabled {"pool":"d-pool-23","added_gpus":14} (audit)

maria: scaling policy updated. new max nodes 120, cooldown 30s. watching node join.

sre-lead: next: tenant throttles for ACME/BetaCorp and restrict unauth'd keys.

alex: applying tenant quotas:
```
redwoodctl quota set --tenant acme --qps 60 --duration 3600
redwoodctl quota set --tenant betacorp --qps 40 --duration 3600
```

alex: ACME quota applied (200 OK).

ryan: patching gateway to add route rate-limit for non-SLA:
```
api-gw set-rate-limit --route "/v1/generate" --limit 180r/s --scope global-non-sla
```
ryan: applied. enterprise keys excluded by ACL.

cs-ops-bot: notifying ACME & BetaCorp contacts about degraded perf and temporary throttle (template dispatched).

alex: also pushing fallback for non-sla to smaller model to reduce tail latency:
```
redwoodctl route update --route "/v1/generate" --fallback-model rwd-1b --condition "not tenant in (acme, betacorp)"
```

alex: fallback rule active.

oncall-bot: metric snapshot 03:25 UTC: 5xx rate down to 3.1% (from 8%), p95 latency down from 1.2s to 0.48s, queue depth trending down.

maria: nodes: ~12 new nodes joined but node-7 & node-11 showing kernel OOM warnings. SSHing to node-7 to inspect.

maria: node-7 logs show heavy cache thrash and a model reload retry loop causing repeated memory spikes. temporary mitigation: restrict concurrent model reloads on node-7.

maria: applying:
```
redwoodctl node set node-7 --reload-concurrency 1
```

maria: applied, model loads stabilized on that host.

sre-lead: ACME/BetaCorp still seeing some 5xxs for long prompts (>2048 tokens)?

ryan: ACME CS reports long prompts (>2048) experiencing degraded success. sent request to apply token-length cap for ACME.

alex: applying token cap policy for ACME:
```
redwoodctl policy create cap-acme-length --tenant acme --max-tokens 2048 --duration 3600
```

alex: policy active.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: primary oncall @alex until 04:00 UTC, then @maria takes over. Incident severity raised to SEV2 while mitigation in flight.

alex: handoff notes: burst enabled (+14 GPUs), max nodes +20 (to 120), cooldown 30s, ACME/BetaCorp QPS caps, global non-sla rate-limit 180r/s, fallback to rwd-1b for non-sla, ACME token cap 2048. Autoscale logs: /var/log/redwood/autoscale/d-pool-23/2026-03-15.log

maria: taking over at 04:00 UTC. will monitor for 2h. if errors >1% re-evaluate disabling large-model route for non-sla.

sre-lead: note cost impact: burst added 14 GPUs ~ +$4.2k/hr. OK short-term due to customer impact, file cost reconciliation.

oncall-bot: update 03:47 UTC: 5xx rate steady at 1.1%, p95 0.35s, queue depth <500. Autoscale stabilized at 98 nodes.

ryan: informing billing & account teams for ACME/BetaCorp about throttles and mitigation. ETA full normalization 30-45m if no new burst.

alex: filing follow-up ticket INF-2134 for autoscaler fragmentation root-cause and initial triage. assigning to eng-runtime.

sre-lead: also add Optimize eval for ACME workload to recommend aggressive prefix/KV caching and smaller-quantized variants.

cs-ops-bot: ACME replies: "Thanks — seeing improved performance. We'll move large backfills offline for the next hour." :white_check_mark:

maria: admin: I'll revert temporary caps after 1 hour if stable. leaving incident thread open for regression alerts.

oncall-bot: incident timeline recorded. status: mitigation successful; monitoring. severity SEV2 -> monitoring.

alex: thanks all. brief retro notes to #postmortems after RCA. :coffee:
